statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let u_0, u_1, ..., u_{m-1} be the values of r in order from its head. Then m = n, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, u_i = v_{j(i)}, where j(i) is defined by j(i) = if i = n-k then k-1 else if i = k-1 then n-k else i. In words, r is exactly the list obtained from head by swapping the value at 0-based position k-1 with the value at 0-based position n-k, leaving every other value and the list length unchanged.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, v_1, ..., v_{n-1} in order from the head (0-indexed). k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n. Every v_i satisfies 0 <= v_i <= 100.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail (no failed Result, overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n nodes and values v_0, v_1, ..., v_{n-1} in order from the head (0-indexed), where 1 <= n <= 100000. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n. Every v_i satisfies 0 <= v_i <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the number of nodes of r is exactly n, the number of nodes of head.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r has n nodes and its values u_0, ..., u_{n-1} satisfy u_i = v_i for every i with 0 <= i < n. That is, r equals head.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n, and k-1 = n-k (equivalently 2*k = n+1).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with values u_0, ..., u_{n-1}, for every i with 0 <= i < n such that i != k-1 and i != n-k, we have u_i = v_i.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with values u_0, ..., u_{n-1}, the value at position k-1 is the original kth-from-end value: u_{k-1} = v_{n-k}.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with values u_0, ..., u_{n-1}, the value at position n-k is the original kth-from-beginning value: u_{n-k} = v_{k-1}.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer x, the number of nodes of r whose value is x equals the number of nodes of head whose value is x. Thus r is a permutation of the values of head.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with values u_0, ..., u_{n-1}, we have u_0 = v_{n-1}, u_{n-1} = v_0, and u_i = v_i for every i with 0 < i < n-1.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n, and either k = 1 or k = n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with values u_0, ..., u_{n-1}, we have u_i = v_i for every i with 0 <= i < n. That is, r equals head.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n. The two selected values are equal: v_{k-1} = v_{n-k}.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with values u_0, ..., u_{n-1}, for every i with 0 <= i < n, u_i != v_i if and only if i = k-1 or i = n-k.
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n. The two selected positions are distinct: k-1 != n-k. The two selected original values are distinct: v_{k-1} != v_{n-k}.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every node value of r is an integer in the interval [0, 100].
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n. Every node value of head is between 0 and 100 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with values u_0, ..., u_{n-1}, the head value u_0 satisfies: u_0 = v_{n-1} if k = 1 or k = n, and u_0 = v_0 otherwise (that is, if 1 < k < n).
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with values u_0, ..., u_{n-1}, the last value u_{n-1} satisfies: u_{n-1} = v_0 if k = 1 or k = n, and u_{n-1} = v_{n-1} otherwise (that is, if 1 < k < n).
preconditions: head is a finite singly linked list with n >= 1 nodes and values v_0, ..., v_{n-1}. k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n.
